notes: Source units are primary. A 'converted' block is added only where useful; its 'conversion' field states how it was obtained.
PIO2 is INSPIRED (humidified) O2 partial pressure, not ambient ppO2: PIO2 = (PB - 47) * FIO2, PB in mmHg (NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2, Table 6.2-1 header). 1 psia = 51.715 mmHg.
Values from conference papers are program baselines of their time, not agency standards; see each entry's 'caveat'.

not_found.item: An agency-level NASA standard that sets a maximum cabin O2 fraction for flammability in exploration habitats
not_found.tried: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 ch.6 (sets diluent >= 30% for atelectasis, not a flammability cap; says OSHA's 23.5% enriched limit 'is more applicable to material flammability'); NTRS searches for NASA-STD-6001 at 34%/8.2 psia; NESC webbing briefs (report material MOCs, not a cabin cap). NASA-STD-6001B is a test method: materials are tested in the worst-case expected atmosphere of each vehicle, so the cap is set per program. Best available: Constellation baselines 30% (Orion) and 34% (LSAM) from NTRS 20070018178, marked as program baselines.
